name: Oat Cookies
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl until very smooth.
Stir in the melted coconut oil and maple syrup.
Add the oats, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt. Mix until fully combined.
Scoop tablespoon-sized rounds onto the sheet and press gently to flatten.
Bake 12–15 min until the edges are golden.
Cool on the pan 5 min, then move to a rack. Cool completely before storing.
Fridge in an airtight container (5 days) or freeze individually (2 weeks).
prepSteps: Bake a full batch and cool completely.
Store in the fridge (5 days) or freeze on a plate so they don't stick together.

name: Zucchini Muffins
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line or grease a muffin tin (avocado oil works).
[WET] Grate the zucchini and squeeze it in a clean towel until very dry — about 1 cup shredded.
[WET] Whisk the zucchini, applesauce, mashed bananas, and eggs together.
[DRY] In a separate bowl, mix the oat flour, baking soda, baking powder, and pumpkin pie spice. Almond flour can stand in for oat flour if running low.
Fold the dry mix into the wet until just combined. Don't overmix.
Fill each cup about ¾ full.
Bake 22–28 min, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool completely on a rack, then bag individually and freeze.
prepSteps: Bake a full batch and cool completely.
Freeze individually on a sheet pan, then transfer to a freezer bag.

name: Pumpkin Oat Muffins
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line the muffin tin or grease it with avocado oil.
[WET] Whisk the pumpkin puree, applesauce, mashed bananas, and eggs together.
[DRY] In a separate bowl, mix the oat flour, baking soda, baking powder, and pumpkin pie spice.
Fold the dry mix into the wet until just combined. Don't overmix.
Fill each cup about ¾ full.
Bake 22–28 min, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool completely on a rack before bagging.
prepSteps: Bake a full batch and cool completely.
Freeze individually on a sheet pan, then transfer to a freezer bag.

name: Egg Muffins
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a standard muffin tin.
Dice the bell pepper and cut the broccoli into small florets.
Whisk the eggs, then stir in the pepper and broccoli.
Pour into the tin — fills about 6 cups.
Bake 18–20 min until set in the center.
Cool, then store in the fridge or freeze in a bag.
prepSteps: Bake a batch and cool. Fridge for the week or freeze.

name: Sweet Potato Rounds
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Slice the sweet potatoes into ½-inch coins.
Toss with avocado oil and a pinch of salt. Spread in a single layer on a lined sheet pan.
Roast 20 min, flipping once.
Cool and store in a fridge container — lasts 4–5 days.
prepSteps: Roast a batch, cool, and store in a fridge container for snacks all week.

name: Roasted Baby Potatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash the potatoes and halve them (slice larger ones).
Toss with avocado oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper. Spread on a sheet pan.
Roast 25–30 min, flipping halfway, until golden and fork-tender.
Cool completely and store in a covered fridge container. Reheat at 375°F for 10 min before serving.
prepSteps: Fully roast, cool, and store in the fridge as a side for dinners.

name: Smoked Lemon Garlic Salmon
instructions: Late afternoon: unwrap the brined salmon and rinse thoroughly under cold water — unrinsed is too salty. Pat dry.
Set skin-side down on a wire rack over a sheet pan and refrigerate uncovered about 2 hours to form a pellicle.
Preheat the Traeger to 225°F (alder or fruitwood pellets).
Place the salmon skin-side down directly on the grate. Smoke 45–60 min until it reaches 145°F internal.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon.
Reheat the roasted potatoes at 375°F for 10 min while the salmon rests, and sauté the frozen vegetables.
prepSteps: [DRY BRINE] Mix the coconut sugar, kosher salt, and black pepper in a small bowl.
Lay a large sheet of plastic wrap on a sheet pan, big enough to wrap the salmon. Spread half the brine on it in the shape of the fillets.
Place the salmon skin-side down on the brine and spread the rest over the top. Wrap tightly.
Set another sheet pan on top with a few cans to weigh it down. Refrigerate.
Halve the baby potatoes, toss with avocado oil and salt, and roast at 400°F for 25–30 min. Cool and refrigerate.

name: Smoked Chicken Fajitas
instructions: Preheat the Traeger to 225°F (hickory or mesquite pellets).
Place the whole marinated breasts directly on the grate.
Smoke 60–75 min until 165°F internal. Keep the breasts whole — they shred easily after resting.
Toss the sliced peppers and onion in avocado oil and add in a foil pan for the last 30 min.
Rest 10 min, then shred with forks.
Warm the corn tortillas on the grate about 30 sec per side. Serve with avocado and a lime wedge.
prepSteps: [MARINADE] In a large zip bag, mix the juice of 3 limes, cumin, chili powder, minced garlic, and avocado oil.
Add the chicken breasts, seal, and massage the marinade in. Refrigerate (holds Thu–Sat).
Slice the bell peppers and onion into strips; bag and refrigerate.

name: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Spread the marinated chicken strips, peppers, and onion on a sheet pan in a single layer.
Roast 25–30 min until the chicken is cooked through and the peppers are soft.
Serve in warm corn tortillas with avocado.
prepSteps: Slice the chicken breasts into strips.
[MARINADE] Toss the chicken with avocado oil, cumin, chili powder, lime juice, salt, and pepper. Refrigerate covered.
Slice the bell peppers and onion into strips; store in the same or a separate container.
